The manipulation of time in the story is exceptionally well-balanced and serves the thematic arc of the narrative. The author uses **compression of time** masterfully to convey an eighteen-month ordeal (plus eleven years of backstory and an autumn epilogue) within a short story. 

At the beginning of the repairs (October through February), the pacing is slightly slower, lingering on specific details, sounds, and departmental conflicts to establish the disruptive nature of the construction. However, once the narrator notes in March that "what we did, mostly, was adapt," the story compresses time much more rapidly ("Spring break came and went. Late summer came and went. The plastic sheeting yellowed and was replaced..."). This acceleration mirrors the psychological reality of the characters: as the suffering becomes routine ("décor"), the months blur together. Finally, the story slows down again to stretch out a single, quiet moment in the corridor on a rainy autumn day, giving emotional weight and resonance to the ending.
